preconditions.description: The number of strings `n` is an integer between 2 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(p_i) >= 1 for p_i in p_list) and all(all(c.islower() for c in p_i) for p_i in p_list)
preconditions.description: Each string `p_i` is non-empty and consists only of lowercase English letters.
The total length of all strings `p_i` is at most 100,000.

postconditions.description: The output is the beauty of the product string, defined as the length of the longest substring consisting of a single repeated character in the product string.

postconditions.expression: max_beauty == max(len(list(group)) for _, group in itertools.groupby(product_string))
postconditions.description: The beauty is computed as the maximum length of any contiguous block of identical characters in the product string, where `product_string` is the result of sequentially multiplying all strings `p_1, p_2, ..., p_n` using Denis's multiplication rule.

postconditions.expression: product_string == reduce(lambda acc, p_i: multiply_strings(acc, p_i), p_list, '')
postconditions.description: The product string is constructed by sequentially applying the multiplication rule: `multiply_strings(s, t) = t + s[0] + t + s[1] + ... + t + s[-1] + t` for strings `s` and `t`.
